lessons.title: Timing of Harvest
lessons.body:
Harvest mushrooms at the right stage for best taste, shelf life, and price. For oyster mushrooms, harvest when the caps are still curled downward and the edges are smooth, not flat or upturned. This is usually 3 to 5 days after the pins appear. For button mushrooms, harvest when the caps are closed and white, before the veil breaks. If you wait too long, the caps open, spores drop, and the mushrooms become tough and lose weight. In Africa, where heat speeds up growth, check your crop twice a dayâmorning and evening. A mushroom can go from perfect to overripe in just 6 hours during hot weather.

Harvest in the cool of the morning or late evening. Avoid the midday sun because mushrooms wilt quickly. Use a sharp, clean knife or twist and pull gently. For oyster mushrooms, cut the whole cluster at the base with a knife. For button mushrooms, twist and pull individually, then trim the stem. Handle mushrooms gentlyâbruises turn brown and reduce quality. Place harvested mushrooms in a clean basket or crate lined with paper or cloth. Do not pile them more than 15 cm deep to prevent crushing and heat buildup.

After harvest, keep mushrooms in a cool, shaded place. If you cannot sell or process them within 2 hours, refrigerate at 2â4Â°C. In rural areas without electricity, use a cool room, a clay pot evaporative cooler, or a shady ventilated shed. Harvest only what you can handle within 2 hours. For a small farm, 5 kg per day is manageable. For larger farms, stagger harvests and have a cold room or buyer ready. Remember: every hour at 30Â°C reduces shelf life by one day. So timing is not just about sizeâit's about keeping your mushrooms fresh and profitable.

lessons.title: Harvesting Tools and Techniques
lessons.body:
You don't need expensive tools to harvest mushrooms, but you need the right ones. A sharp, thin-bladed knife (like a paring knife or a small kitchen knife) is essential. For oyster mushrooms, you cut the whole cluster at the base. For button mushrooms, you twist and pull, then trim the stem with the knife. Avoid using a machete or dull knifeâthey crush the mushroom and leave it open to rot. Always clean your knife with 70% alcohol or bleach solution (1 tablespoon per litre of water) between beds to prevent disease spread.

Use clean baskets or crates for harvesting. Plastic crates with ventilation holes are best. Line them with clean paper or cloth to cushion the mushrooms. Do not use sacks or bucketsâthey squash the mushrooms and trap heat. For every 5 kg of mushrooms, use a crate that is at least 30 cm x 40 cm and 15 cm deep. Harvest with both hands: one to hold the cluster, one to cut. Twist and pull button mushrooms gently, holding the cap, not the stem. If you pull too hard, you damage the mycelium and reduce the next flush.

After cutting, trim the stem to 1â2 cm and remove any substrate or dirt. Place mushrooms in the crate with the caps up. Do not wash mushrooms at harvestâwashing adds water and shortens shelf life. Instead, clean later with a soft brush or damp cloth. For farms with many workers, train everyone to use the same technique. A 10% bruise rate can drop your price by 20%. Also, harvest in the cool hours and move crates to shade immediately. If you harvest 20 kg per day, you need at least 4 crates and a shaded collection point. Keep tools clean and sharpâa dull knife is a farmer's worst enemy.

lessons.title: Cleaning and Sorting
lessons.body:
After harvest, clean mushrooms gently. Do not soak them in waterâthey absorb water like sponges and become soggy. Instead, use a soft brush or a clean damp cloth to wipe off substrate, soil, or bits of straw. For oyster mushrooms, you can peel off the base if it's dirty. For button mushrooms, wipe the cap and trim the stem. If mushrooms are very dirty, a quick dip in cold water for 10 seconds, then pat dry with a clean cloth, is acceptable. But never leave them in water. Clean mushrooms look better and sell faster.

Sorting means separating mushrooms by size, shape, and quality. Remove any mushrooms that are bruised, torn, discolored, or have signs of mold or insects. These can be used for home consumption or processing, but not for fresh sale. Sort into three groups: Grade A (perfect, uniform size, no blemishes), Grade B (slightly imperfect but good for cooking), and Grade C (for processing or animal feed). For oyster mushrooms, Grade A clusters are 10â15 cm across, with caps 5â8 cm wide. For button mushrooms, Grade A caps are 2â4 cm in diameter, closed, and white.

Sorting increases your income. Grade A fetches 30â50% more than mixed mushrooms. In local markets, a kilogram of sorted Grade A oyster mushrooms can sell for 2â3 times the price of unsorted. Do sorting in a cool, shaded area, not in the sun. Use clean tables and clean hands. Wear gloves if possible. After sorting, pack immediately into clean containers. If you are selling to hotels or supermarkets, they will demand consistent grading. So practice sorting from day one. Even a small farm of 50 bags can produce 10 kg per weekâsorting that 10 kg well can add 20â30% to your revenue.

lessons.title: Grading and Packaging
lessons.body:
Grading is sorting by standard sizes and quality. For oyster mushrooms, Grade A: clusters 10â15 cm wide, caps 5â8 cm, no blemishes, uniform color. Grade B: clusters 8â10 cm, caps 3â5 cm, slight blemishes. Grade C: broken or small pieces, for processing. For button mushrooms: Grade A: caps 2â4 cm, closed, white, no spots. Grade B: caps 4â6 cm, slightly open. Grade C: open caps or damaged. Use a simple sizing ring or a ruler to grade. Consistent grading builds trust with buyers and allows you to set higher prices.

Packaging protects mushrooms and makes them attractive. Use clean, ventilated containers. For local markets, small baskets or paper bags with holes work. For supermarkets and hotels, use clear plastic punnets (200g or 500g) wrapped in cling film, or cardboard trays with perforated film. Never use sealed plastic bagsâmushrooms sweat and rot. For 1 kg, use a container about 20 cm x 15 cm x 10 cm. Label with your farm name, weight, and harvest date. In Africa, many buyers prefer 250g or 500g packs. For export, follow the buyer's specifications, often 200g punnets in cartons of 10.

Packaging also affects shelf life. Mushrooms packed in perforated film last 5â7 days at 4Â°C. Without packaging, they dry out or bruise. For transport, stack crates no more than 3 high to avoid crushing. Use a cool box or refrigerated truck if going far. If you sell in a local market, take only what you can sell in one day. For every 10 kg packed, you need about 20 punnets of 500g. Good packaging reduces waste by 20â30% and can increase your price by 10â20%. So invest in clean, proper packagingâit pays back quickly.

lessons.title: Cold Storage and Shelf Life
lessons.body:
Mushrooms are perishable. At room temperature (25â30Â°C), they last only 1â2 days. At 4Â°C, they last 5â7 days. At 0â2Â°C, up to 10 days. So cold storage is critical. If you have electricity, use a refrigerator set at 2â4Â°C. Do not freeze mushroomsâfreezing turns them mushy unless you blanch them first. For small farms, a used refrigerator or a chest freezer converted to a cooler works. For larger farms, a cold room is best. But in rural Africa, electricity is often unreliable. Use evaporative cooling: a clay pot cooler (pot-in-pot) can keep mushrooms at 10â15Â°C, extending shelf life to 3â4 days. A shaded, well-ventilated room with wet sand on the floor can also help.

Store mushrooms in their packagingâperforated punnets or paper bagsânot in sealed containers. Keep them away from strong-smelling foods like onions or fish because mushrooms absorb odors. Do not wash before storage. Check daily and remove any spoiled mushrooms. For maximum shelf life, harvest in the morning, cool quickly, and store immediately. If you sell at a market, take a cooler box with ice packs. For every 5 kg, use 2 ice packs (frozen water bottles work). This keeps mushrooms fresh for 6â8 hours.

Shelf life also depends on handling. Bruised mushrooms spoil faster. So handle gently. If you cannot sell within 3 days, process them (drying, powdering, or canning). Dried mushrooms last 6â12 months. For fresh sales, aim to sell within 2 days. In hot climates, pick early, keep cool, and sell fast. A simple rule: every hour at 30Â°C reduces shelf life by one day. So if you harvest at 6 AM and keep at 30Â°C until noon, you lose half a day. Cold storage is not a luxuryâit's a necessity for profit.

lessons.title: Value Addition (Drying, Powdering)
lessons.body:
Value addition turns fresh mushrooms into products that last longer and sell for more. Drying is the easiest. Slice mushrooms 3â5 mm thick. For oyster mushrooms, separate clusters into individual caps. Spread on clean trays or screens in a well-ventilated, sunny area. Cover with a thin cloth to keep off dust and insects. Sun-drying takes 2â3 days in dry weather. For faster drying, use a solar dryerâa simple box with a glass top and vents. Dry until mushrooms are brittle and snap when bent. Good drying removes 90% of water. From 10 kg fresh, you get about 1 kg dried.

After drying, cool the mushrooms, then pack in airtight containers (glass jars, plastic containers with tight lids, or vacuum-sealed bags). Store in a cool, dark, dry place. Dried mushrooms last 6â12 months. You can sell them whole or grind into powder. To make powder, grind dried mushrooms in a clean blender or mortar and pestle. Sift to remove coarse pieces. Mushroom powder is a flavor enhancer for soups, stews, and sauces. It sells well in urban markets and to restaurants. A 100g jar of mushroom powder can sell for 5â10 times the price of fresh mushrooms.

Other value-added products include pickled mushrooms, mushroom sauce, and mushroom chips. Pickling: boil mushrooms in vinegar, salt, and spices, then pack in jars. Pickled mushrooms last 6â12 months. For a small business, start with drying and powderingâthey need low investment. A solar dryer can cost $50â100, but you can build one with local materials. Packaging is key: use clean, labeled jars or bags. In Africa, dried mushrooms are popular in soups and as a meat substitute. So don't just sell freshâadd value. It reduces waste, increases income, and opens new markets.

lessons.title: Practical Reference
lessons.body:
Practical Reference: Harvesting & Post-Harvest Handling of Mushrooms in Africa

Mushroom farming in Africa is a high-margin, low-land enterprise â but the money is made or lost in the 48 hours after the first cap opens. Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus), shiitake (Lentinula edodes), and button (Agaricus bisporus) mushrooms lose 10â20% of their fresh weight within 24 hours of harvest if handled poorly. For a smallholder in Kenya, Nigeria, Ghana, or Uganda, that is the difference between a profitable cycle and a wasted substrate block. This lesson gives you the practical numbers, tools, and workflows to protect your crop from field to buyer.

1. Timing of Harvest

Harvest mushrooms before the cap fully flattens. For oyster mushrooms, the ideal window is when the cap margin is still slightly curled downward and the gills are white to cream â usually 3â5 days after pinning, depending on temperature. In warm African conditions (24â30Â°C), this window can close in 12â18 hours. Check blocks twice daily: early morning (6â8 am) and late afternoon (4â6 pm).

Harvesting too late causes spore release (brown dust), reduced shelf life, and lower market price. Harvesting too early reduces yield per block. A simple rule: harvest when the cap is 70â90% open for oyster mushrooms, and when the veil is intact but stretching for button mushrooms.

2. Harvesting Tools and Techniques

Use clean, sharp tools. Dull knives bruise the stipe and invite bacterial blotch. Recommended tools:

  • Stainless steel knife or curved harvesting blade
  • Clean cotton gloves (optional but reduces bruising)
  • Ventilated plastic crates (not sacks â sacks crush and heat the crop)
  • Clean cloth or paper towel for wiping tools between blocks

Technique: Grasp the cluster gently, cut at the base of the stipe with a single clean stroke, and place the mushrooms gills down in the crate. Do not pull â pulling damages the substrate and reduces the next flush. For shiitake, twist and pull gently to remove the entire stipe base.

3. Cleaning and Sorting

Do not wash mushrooms with water â they absorb it like sponges and rot within hours. Instead, brush off substrate particles with a soft brush or clean cloth. Remove any mushrooms with brown spots, insect damage, or slime. Sort by size and appearance immediately after harvest; delays of even 4 hours at 28Â°C reduce quality.

4. Grading and Packaging

Grade according to buyer requirements. Local markets in Nairobi, Lagos, and Accra typically accept three grades:

Table 1: Fresh Mushroom Grading Standards (Oyster & Button)
Grade Cap Size Appearance Typical Buyer Price Index
A (Premium) 4â8 cm, uniform Firm, no blemishes, intact cluster Supermarkets, hotels, export 100%
B (Standard) 3â10 cm, mixed Minor blemishes, slightly open caps Restaurants, local retailers 70â80%
C (Processing) Any size, broken Over-mature, split, or damaged Drying, powdering, soup makers 40â50%

Source: Adapted from FAO (2021) and Kenya Horticultural Crops Development Authority (HCDA) market standards.

Packaging: Use perforated polythene bags (0.5â1% ventilation holes) or punnets with cling film. Pack 250g or 500g units for retail. Label with harvest date, grade, and farm name. For bulk buyers, use ventilated crates lined with clean paper.

5. Cold Storage and Shelf Life

Mushrooms are 90% water and respire continuously. Without cooling, shelf life is 24â48 hours in African ambient conditions. With proper cold storage (2â4Â°C, 85â90% RH), oyster mushrooms last 7â10 days; button mushrooms 10â14 days.

Table 2: Shelf Life by Storage Method and Species
Storage Method Temperature Oyster Button Shiitake
Ambient (open) 25â32Â°C 1 day 1â2 days 2â3 days
Evaporative cooler 15â20Â°C 3â4 days 4â5 days 5â7 days
Refrigerator 2â4Â°C 7â10 days 10â14 days 14â21 days
Dried (10â12% moisture) Ambient, sealed 6â12 months 6â12 months 12â18 months

Source: Adapted from FAO (2021) and Mushroom Council post-harvest data (2022).

â ï¸ SAFETY WARNING â Aflatoxin & Moisture Risk

Improper drying of mushrooms in humid African climates can lead to mould growth and aflatoxin contamination. Never dry mushrooms on bare ground or in open air during rainy season. Use a solar dryer or raised drying rack with good airflow. Dried mushrooms must reach below 12% moisture before storage. Store in airtight, food-grade containers away from sunlight. If you see any green, black, or white fuzzy mould â discard the entire batch. Do not sell or consume mouldy dried mushrooms. Aflatoxins are heat-stable and cannot be destroyed by cooking.

6. Value Addition: Drying and Powdering

Value addition is where African mushroom farmers can double or triple income. Fresh oyster mushrooms sell for KES 400â600/kg (USD 3â5) in Nairobi. Dried mushrooms sell for KES 2,500â4,000/kg (USD 20â32). Powdered mushroom seasoning sells for even more per kilogram.

Drying methods:

  • Solar dryer: 2â3 days at 45â55Â°C. Best for small-scale. Cost: USD 50â150 locally fabricated.
  • Oven drying: 50â60Â°C for 4â6 hours. Use only if you have reliable power.
  • Sun drying: Only in dry season, on raised racks with mesh. 3â5 days. Risk of contamination.

Powdering: Grind dried mushrooms in a clean blender or hammer mill. Sieve to uniform particle size. Pack in airtight jars or foil pouches. Label with production date and weight. Target markets: supermarkets, spice shops, restaurants, and export to diaspora communities.

Quick Reference Checklist

  1. Harvest at 70â90% cap opening â check blocks twice daily.
  2. Use sharp, clean knife; cut â never pull.
  3. Place mushrooms gills-down in ventilated crates.
  4. Never wash with water â brush clean instead.
  5. Grade into A, B, C within 2 hours of harvest.
  6. Pack in perforated bags; label with date and grade.
  7. Cool to 2â4Â°C within 4 hours if possible; otherwise sell within 24 hours.
  8. Dry excess crop to below 12% moisture; store airtight.

Further Reading

  • FAO â Mushroom Cultivation for Smallholders (PDF)
  • FAO â Small-scale Mushroom Production and Processing
  • Kenya Horticultural Crops Development Authority (HCDA) â Market Standards
  • Nigeria â National Information and Documentation Centre (NIFAD) Mushroom Resources
  • Mushroom Council â Post-Harvest Handling & Storage Data

Business note: In Africa, the highest-margin mushroom businesses are not the growers â they are the processors and packagers. A farmer selling fresh mushrooms earns USD 3â5/kg. A farmer who dries, powders, and brands earns USD 20â40/kg. Invest in a solar dryer and a grinder before you expand your growing room.

quiz.q: When is the best time to harvest oyster mushrooms?
options: A) When caps are fully flat and upturned
B) When caps are still curled downward and edges smooth
D) When stems are very long
quiz.explanation: Oyster mushrooms are best harvested when caps are still curled downward and edges are smooth, before they flatten or upturn.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid harvesting mushrooms in the midday sun?
options: A) Mushrooms grow faster in sun
B) Mushrooms wilt quickly and lose quality
quiz.explanation: Midday sun causes mushrooms to wilt and lose quality due to heat and moisture loss.

quiz.q: What is the maximum recommended depth for piling harvested mushrooms in a basket?
quiz.explanation: Piling deeper than 15 cm can crush mushrooms and cause heat buildup.

quiz.q: How long can mushrooms be kept at room temperature (25-30Â°C) before quality drops significantly?
quiz.explanation: At room temperature, mushrooms last only 1-2 days before spoiling.

quiz.q: Which tool is best for harvesting oyster mushrooms?
quiz.explanation: A sharp thin-bladed knife cleanly cuts clusters without crushing.

quiz.q: How should you clean your knife between harvesting different mushroom beds?
options: C) Wipe with 70% alcohol or bleach solution
quiz.explanation: Alcohol or bleach solution disinfects the knife to prevent disease spread.

quiz.q: What is the recommended size of a crate for 5 kg of mushrooms?
options: A) 10 cm x 10 cm x 5 cm
B) 30 cm x 40 cm x 15 cm
C) 50 cm x 50 cm x 30 cm
D) 20 cm x 20 cm x 10 cm
quiz.explanation: A crate of about 30 cm x 40 cm x 15 cm holds 5 kg without crushing.

quiz.q: Why should you not wash mushrooms immediately after harvest?
options: B) It adds water and shortens shelf life
quiz.explanation: Washing adds water, which promotes spoilage and reduces shelf life.

quiz.q: What is the best way to remove dirt from mushrooms before sale?
options: B) Use a soft brush or damp cloth
quiz.explanation: A soft brush or damp cloth cleans without adding excess water.

quiz.q: How many grades are commonly used for sorting mushrooms?
quiz.explanation: Common grading is Grade A, B, and C based on quality and size.

quiz.q: What is the typical size of Grade A oyster mushroom caps?
quiz.explanation: Grade A oyster mushroom caps are typically 5-8 cm wide.

quiz.q: How much more can Grade A mushrooms fetch compared to mixed grades?
quiz.explanation: Grade A mushrooms can sell for 30-50% more than mixed grades.

quiz.q: What type of packaging is best for fresh mushrooms?
options: B) Ventilated containers or perforated film
quiz.explanation: Ventilated packaging prevents sweating and spoilage.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid sealed plastic bags for fresh mushrooms?
quiz.explanation: Sealed bags trap moisture, causing mushrooms to sweat and rot.

quiz.q: What information should be on a mushroom package label?
options: A) Farm name, weight, harvest date
quiz.explanation: Labeling with farm name, weight, and harvest date builds trust and traceability.

quiz.q: How long do mushrooms last at 4Â°C?
quiz.explanation: At 4Â°C, mushrooms last about 5-7 days.

quiz.q: What is the ideal storage temperature for fresh mushrooms?
quiz.explanation: 2-4Â°C is ideal for fresh mushrooms to maximize shelf life.

quiz.q: What is a pot-in-pot cooler used for?
quiz.explanation: A pot-in-pot cooler uses evaporation to keep mushrooms cool without electricity.

quiz.q: How can you keep mushrooms fresh during market transport without refrigeration?
options: A) Use ice packs in a cooler box
quiz.explanation: Ice packs in a cooler box maintain low temperature during transport.

quiz.q: What is the first step in drying mushrooms?
quiz.explanation: Slicing to 3-5 mm thickness ensures even and fast drying.

quiz.q: How long does sun-drying mushrooms take in dry weather?
quiz.explanation: Sun-drying typically takes 2-3 days in dry, sunny weather.

quiz.q: What is the approximate yield of dried mushrooms from 10 kg fresh?
quiz.explanation: Drying removes about 90% water, so 10 kg fresh yields about 1 kg dried.

quiz.q: How should dried mushrooms be stored?
options: B) In airtight containers in a cool, dark place
D) In paper bags in sunlight
quiz.explanation: Airtight containers in cool, dark, dry conditions prevent moisture and spoilage.

quiz.q: What is mushroom powder used for?
options: B) Flavor enhancer in soups and stews
quiz.explanation: Mushroom powder is a popular flavor enhancer for various dishes.

quiz.q: How long do pickled mushrooms last?
quiz.explanation: Properly pickled mushrooms can last 6-12 months.

quiz.q: What is a key benefit of value addition?
options: A) Reduces waste and increases income
quiz.explanation: Value addition reduces waste and allows selling at higher prices.

quiz.q: What is the recommended thickness for slicing mushrooms for drying?
quiz.explanation: 3-5 mm slices dry evenly and quickly.

quiz.q: Why should you cover sun-drying mushrooms with a thin cloth?
options: B) To keep off dust and insects
quiz.explanation: A thin cloth protects from dust and insects while allowing air circulation.

quiz.q: What is a solar dryer?
options: A) A box with glass top and vents
quiz.explanation: A solar dryer uses solar heat with a glass top and vents for efficient drying.

quiz.q: How much can a 100g jar of mushroom powder sell for compared to fresh mushrooms?
quiz.explanation: Mushroom powder can sell for 5-10 times the price of fresh mushrooms per weight.
